messages.subject: Geography file not read correctly
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm just trying to run a simple, unstratified analysis. However, my biogeography file is not being read properly. I don't get an error message when I upload the file, but it clear from the states at the terminal tips of the tree in the output that something is wrong. It seems that the all the states that I coded in the biogeography file are being read as a different state, shifted over by 1.

For example, the order is "New World, Palearctic, Africa, Madagascar...", and the species I specify as "Madagascar" are coming out as "Africa". The species I coded as "Africa" are considered "Palearctic". This is a screenshot from some of the output below:

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-ce9SYQPqA0o/WsRkIVwR02I/AAAAAAAAAlQ/2SoG4aZCQbUcpHpQp4To1TixHx59Tr_ggCLcBGAs/s1600/Screen%2BShot%2B2018-04-03%2Bat%2B11.29.55%2BPM.png>

My geography file is in phylip format and has a tab in between the number of species and the number of states. I included pertinent code, the tree file, and the biogeography file to this post. Has anyone else had this problem?

Thank you in advance!

Jenna

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Geography file not read correctly
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

The issue is that if you change include_null_range to FALSE in the model inputs, you also have to change it in the graphing function, compare the example script:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script

===============
results_object = resDEC
scriptdir = np(system.file("extdata/a_scripts", package="BioGeoBEARS"))

# States
res2 = plot_BioGeoBEARS_results(results_object, analysis_titletxt, addl_params=list("j"), plotwhat="text", label.offset=0.45, tipcex=0.7, statecex=0.7, splitcex=0.6, titlecex=0.8, plotsplits=TRUE, cornercoords_loc=scriptdir, include_null_range=TRUE, tr=tr, tipranges=tipranges)

# Pie chart
plot_BioGeoBEARS_results(results_object, analysis_titletxt, addl_params=list("j"), plotwhat="pie", label.offset=0.45, tipcex=0.7, statecex=0.7, splitcex=0.6, titlecex=0.8, plotsplits=TRUE, cornercoords_loc=scriptdir, include_null_range=TRUE, tr=tr, tipranges=tipranges)
===============

...to...
===============
results_object = resDEC
scriptdir = np(system.file("extdata/a_scripts", package="BioGeoBEARS"))

# States
res2 = plot_BioGeoBEARS_results(results_object, analysis_titletxt, addl_params=list("j"), plotwhat="text", label.offset=0.45, tipcex=0.7, statecex=0.7, splitcex=0.6, titlecex=0.8, plotsplits=TRUE, cornercoords_loc=scriptdir, include_null_range=FALSE, tr=tr, tipranges=tipranges)

# Pie chart
plot_BioGeoBEARS_results(results_object, analysis_titletxt, addl_params=list("j"), plotwhat="pie", label.offset=0.45, tipcex=0.7, statecex=0.7, splitcex=0.6, titlecex=0.8, plotsplits=TRUE, cornercoords_loc=scriptdir, include_null_range=FALSE, tr=tr, tipranges=tipranges)
===============

...without doing that, everything will be offset by 1 range, because the null range always comes first in the list of ranges, if it exists.

Also note that include_null_range=FALSE creates the DEC-star (DEC*) model, DEC*+J, etc.  This can have dramatic and unintuitive impacts, read Massana et al. on bioRxiv, and google my comments on PhyloWiki/the Google Group.  The key thing is for you to understand what the model variations are doing and why and be able to explain your choices in the eventual paper/thesis/etc.

Cheers!
Nick

messages.subject: When the LnL are "significantly" equal, do I use AIC or AICc?
messages.subject_clean: When the LnL are "significantly" equal, do I use AIC or AICc?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I did a BioGeoBEARS analysis to estimate the ancestral area for night monkeys and understand what the main factors (like extinction, dispersal, founder, etc.) that acted in their diversification history.

I found DIVALIKE and DIVALIKE-J as the best models to explain the biogeographical history of this genus.

Although DIVALIKE-J has a lower LnL value than DIVALIKE, it was not significant (p value = 0.14). However, the DIVALIKE-J has AIC value of 59.08, while DIVALIKE has an AIC value of 59.28. The AIC weight of DIVALIKE-J was 0.35 and for DIVALIKE was 0.32.

However, when I looked the the AICc, the DIVALIKE showed a much lower value of 61.68 and DIVALIKE-J showed an AICc value of 65.08. The AICc weight values were 0.6 for DIVALIKE and 0.11 for DIVALIKE-J

My question is relatively simple (or not...):

- Should I consider the AIC or AICc values?

The values are very close and I think that both of them are reasonable to explain the biogeographical history of night monkeys. However, in a biological and geological perspective, the DIVALIKE-J seems to be more acceptable.

Can somebody help me?

Best regards,
Antonio.

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] When the LnL are "significantly" equal, do I use AIC or AICc?
messages.subject_clean: [BioGeoBEARS] When the LnL are "significantly" equal, do I use AIC or AICc?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Antonio!

AICc is designed for small datasets, the "c" is a bias correction for small AIC at sample sizes.   Here you have 8 species, so n=8, a very small dataset size.  So, a journal would want you to report the AICc results (you could also report AIC if you want).

Ideally, I like to have at least 5-10 data per free parameter (ideally more) - it becomes very hard to get any signal to distinguish models if the number of data per free parameter is low.

As for interpretation, it doesn't matter much which one comes out on top, the main message of those results is that the models are not very different in fitting the data. AIC/AICc is a sliding scale, the statistical philosophy is entirely different from the frequentist statistical philosophy that relies on p-value cutoffs, or "statistical significance".  See here:

Interpreting delta-AICs/differences in AIC: Some handy graphics from Burnham, Anderson, & Huyvaert (2011)
http://phylo.wikidot.com/advice-on-statistical-model-comparison-in-biogeobears#interpreting_deltaAICs

As for choosing a model, in my view you can present anything in a paper as long as you explain why.

Good: "With small data, it is expected that there will be lower power to distinguish models. We observed this here, with an AICc difference of only xxx. Both models gave similar histories, but we chose to present the DIVALIKE+J results in Figure 1 on the basis of prior information XYZ. The results under DIVALIKE are available in Supp Figure 1."

Bad: "DIVALIKE+J outperforms DIVALIKE under AIC by 0.3 units, leading to a relative model weight of 55%:45%. Therefore, we are certain DIVALIKE+J is the best model and are presenting these stunning results based on 8 data points as a revolutionary, highly significant confirmation of hypothesis X."

See also:

Advice On Statistical Model Comparison In Biogeobears
http://phylo.wikidot.com/advice-on-statistical-model-comparison-in-biogeobears

Cheers!
Nick

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] +J model causing R to crash
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

There haven't been any updates that touched this area.

The only thing I've ever heard/noticed about this, mostly several years ago, is that sometimes BAYAREALIKE or BAYAREALIKE+J crashes, typically on Windows machines.

The main solutions are/were:

1. Narrow the parameter limits a bit -- e.g. after setting up the model, check/edit the parameters table:

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table

- change the "min" for j from 0.00001 to 0.001
- change the "min" for d from 0.000000000001 (whatever it is) to 0.001

...this seems to help avoid numeric underflow problems on some machines.

2. There is a newish option as well, which, if a particular combination of parameter values causes a NaN error (Not A Number), will replace the NaN likelihood with a low value, allowing the Maximum Likelihood search to continue without crashing.

Again, before running the search, set this default minimum log-likelihood like this:

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$on_NaN_error = -1e50

Cheers,
Nick
